end.summary:
- Exact values were practised for situations such as school fees and bank balances; approximate values for large crowds and headlines were practised, with a why or new situation still to check.
- Rounding large numbers to lakh and crore was practised; several answers were right, but the choice of place was not steady yet.
- The size of rounding error was practised using totals: 1,196 versus 1,000, a difference of ₹196; this still needs checking in new examples.
- A chain-rounding mix-up (3,45,000 → 3,50,000 → 4,00,000) was seen and was not corrected after it was last seen.
end.parentNote: Asha practised choosing exact or approximate values, rounding to lakh and crore, and comparing a rounded total with the original total. Ayaan used relevant reasons for exact fees and balances and approximate crowd counts and headlines; they also calculated the ₹196 difference in one total. The chain-rounding mix-up was not corrected after it was last seen. At home, give one number at a time and ask Ayaan to name the rounding place, round it once, and estimate the possible error.
